sentences.text:
This petition is preferred by the petitioner/accused No.1 seeking to quash the docket order dated 24.01.2025 passed in C.C.No.1200 of 2017 on the file of the learned II Additional Junior Civil Judge,
Karimnagar, registered for the offences under Sections 420 and 409 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'I.P.C.').

entities.text:
II Additional Junior Civil Judge,
Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter referred as arrayed in C.C.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that on 28.03.2016 the complainant/LW.1 lodged a complaint stating that the office of Registrar, Karimnagar is attached with Stamp Counter to vend stamps to the needy public, for vending of stamps a Junior Assistant and a Shroff are appointed, certain instructions were given to them to maintain the records in the stamp counter.

According to requirement the office of Registrar place indent to District Registrar, get the stocks and the same are kept in the stamp counter under the custody of Junior Assistant and Shroff allotted to maintain the stamp counter.

There are different kinds of stamps, franking machine sales, Indian Revenue tickets,
court fee lables etc., for sale in the counter, they are sold by cash or on submission of challans, the cash id deposited in the account of Sub-Registrar, Karimnagar on the next day of sale, in turn on the another day the smae is transferred to Government account, the entire maintenance of stamp counter is looked after by the Junior Assistant and Shroff allotted to the counter.
Smt K.Anusha Junior Assitant is working since 07.10.2013 and N.Gangalath Shroff is working since 29.06.2012 in the stamp counter in RO, Karimnagar.
During the course of verification of stocks in the stamp counter some variation was noticed.

Immediately the complainant brought the same to the notice of the District Registrar, Karimnagar, in turn as per the instructions of District Registrar, Karimnagar a Committee comprising of Joint Sub- Registrars, Jagtial, Bheemadevarapalli, Senior Assistant and Junior Assistant o/o DIG (R&S), Karimnagar was constituted for verification of sale of stamps with remitttance and physical stock with ledger of stamp counter in RO (OB), Karimnagar for the period from 01.01.2013 to elict the truth and also to fish out the factual facts and the employees who are responsible for the lapses noticed if any.
Accordingly the committee enquired into the matter by verifying the concerned records for RO (OB), Karimnagar.

During the course of verification the committee had taken-up the activities of receipt of stocks supplied to the office, all the sales, closing stock physically available in the office and noticed deviations in respect of maintenance of stock, sale and in remittance in the following categories.

4. It is also noticed that an amount of Rs.18,52,970/- was misappropriated in embossing of Franking impressions through franking machine maintained in the office, the concerned Junior Assistant and shroff who dealt the sales have made these franking impressions on different dates for various amounts, but they did not remit the said amount in the account of the Joint Sub-Registrar-I for onward transfer of the same to the Government Treasury.

The concerned Junior Assistant and Shroff further with a fraudulent and dishonest intention made wrong entries in the sales register as if sold away the stocks on production of challans by the parties, though the parties did not produce the challans as no challans available in the records, they further committed malpractice and manipulations by making factitious challan particulars for some entries.
They further dishonestly made incorrect entries to the amounts franked by them despite the parties produced the challan for lesser amounts.

On physical verification of stock available in the office as on 22.01.2016 in the presence of Joint Sub-Registrars I and II and the concerned Junior Assistant and Shroff who dealt the counter and some other staff members the different kinds of stamps to an amount of Rs.52,23,956/- are found shortage thus the concerned Junior Assistant and Shroff sold the stamps on different dates, did not remit the amount in the account of Joint Sub-Registrar-I for onward transfer to the Government account, thereby misappropriated the amount of Rs.52,23,956/-.

The misappropriated amount is prima facie estimated at Rs.18,52,970/- in sale through franking machine and Rs.52,23,956/-, total amount of Rs.70,76,926/- during the period of 23.11.2013 to 26.08.2015.
5. Basing on the said complaint, Inspector of Police, Karimnagar-I town registered a case in Crime No.129 of 2016, under Sections 420 and 409 of the Indian Penal Code and took up the investigation.

6. Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner/accused No.1 and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State and perused the record.
7.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that on 24.01.2025, the trial Court conducted the examination of the petitioner under Section 239 of Cr.P.C and framed charges against the accused under Section 240 Cr.P.C, without adhering to the mandatory requirements set forth under Section 238 Cr.P.C., specifically the requirement to furnish copies of documents relied upon by the prosecution under Section 207 Cr.P.C was not complied with.

Though the trial Court on 29.01.2025 and 31.01.2025 directed the prosecution to furnish the copies, the prosecution failed to do so and framed the charges against the accused vide docket order dated 24.01.2025.
The petitioner also filed a petition to set aside the examination conducted under Section 239 Cr.P.C.
A copy of application for docket orders was made on 11.02.2025 vide C.A.No.1821 of 2025 and the same was pending.
Hence, the present criminal petition.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State would submit that on the directions of the learned trial Court, necessary documents have been supplied to the petitioner on 24.02.2025.
He would further submit that the trial is under progress and therefore, indulgence of this Court at this stage is unwarranted.
Hence seeks to dismiss the present criminal petition.

9. In the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the prosecution without furnishing the copies of the documents to the petitioner/accused No.1 has framed the charges on 24.01.2025, which is a clear violation of Section 207 of Cr.P.C by the respondent - Police and the trial Court.

Accordingly, this Court deems it appropriate to quash the docket order dated 24.01.2025 in C.C.No.1200 of 2017 on the file of the learned II Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class Judge, Karimnagar.

entities.text: II Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class Judge, Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Since the petitioner/accused No.1 has already been supplied with the necessary documents as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C, the trial Court is directed to conduct the proceedings afresh and pass appropriate order in accordance with law.
10. With the above observations, this Criminal Petition is disposed of.
As a sequel thereto, Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
